examples.question_text:
Write these times as decimal hours.
(a) $5$ h $24$ min
(b) $47$ min
examples.solution_text:
Divide minutes by $60$ and add any whole hours.
(a) $5+\frac{24}{60}=5.4$ h.
(b) $\frac{47}{60}=0.78\dot3$ h. The $3$ repeats; keep this exact recurring decimal.

examples.question_text: Convert $3$ h $12$ min $45$ s to decimal hours.
examples.solution_text:
Divide minutes by $60$ and seconds by $3600$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3+\frac{12}{60}+\frac{45}{3600}\\&=3+0.2+0.0125\\&=3.2125\text{ h}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Write these times in hours and minutes.
(a) $6.35$ h
(b) $0.65$ h
examples.solution_text:
Keep any whole hours; multiply the decimal part by $60$.
(a) $0.35\times60=21$ min, so $6.35$ h $=6$ h $21$ min.
(b) $0.65\times60=39$ min, so $0.65$ h $=39$ min.

examples.question_text: Convert $4.2375$ h to hours, minutes and seconds.
examples.solution_text:
Keep $4$ whole hours.
$0.2375\times60=14.25$ min.
Keep $14$ whole minutes, then convert the remaining fraction:
$0.25\times60=15$ s.
The time is $4$ h $14$ min $15$ s.

examples.question_text:
(a) Convert $2.\dot6$ h to hours and minutes.
(b) Convert $7$ min $30$ s to decimal hours.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $0.\dot6=\frac23$.
$\frac23\times60=40$ min, so $2.\dot6$ h $=2$ h $40$ min.
Keep the exact repeating value instead of rounding it first.
(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac7{60}+\frac{30}{3600}\\&=\frac18\\&=0.125\text{ h}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: 12/60 = 0.2 and 45/3600 = 0.0125, so 3 + 0.2 + 0.0125 = 3.2125 hours. The formatting preserves the original calculation and adds the required phantom equals gutter.

For (a), the exact recurring fractional hour is 2/3; (2/3) × 60 = 40 minutes, giving 2 hours 40 minutes. For (b), 7/60 + 30/3600 = 420/3600 + 30/3600 = 450/3600 = 1/8 = 0.125 hours. Both parts preserve the baseline mathematics.
